correctness.rationale: For a full-square 2D commutative algebra, mu:Sym^2(S)->S is a surjection with 1D kernel; a natural basis (a,b) exists iff the kernel line is a tensor a odot b with independent a,b, equivalently square-free split binary quadratic. This is valid in characteristic 2 because it is symmetric tensor algebra, not square-map polarization. The explicit 3D evolution construction with i(u)=e1+e3, i(v)=e2+e3 and basis squares i(u^2-uv),i(v^2-uv),i(uv) multiplies correctly and has stable square i(S). Projective quadratic factor enumeration gives q(q+1)/2, q+1, q(q-1)/2 kernel lines with |GL_2(q)| quotient isomorphisms. Independent exhaustive q=2,3 counts (18,18,6),(288,192,144), confirms natural-basis test and stable-square realization.
